reader.notes: One class screen (CheckArgumentClasses over the Verified 'n' row) serves every edition; its classifier matches the 1985 class model (numeric-edited and groups are alphanumeric, ZERO is admissible). The diagnostic text cites §2023:15.82.3 r1 even at --std 85, which names the wrong edition's clause but does not change the verdict.

refuter.evidence: Requirement re-derived from §1989:A.2.2 AR1 ('An arithmetic expression must be specified') and §1985:VI.6.2.1 (numeric elementary identifiers, numeric literals, ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, operators, parentheses, unary sign). Accept half, refute-1985-172/q_ok_forms.cob at --std 85 (runs/q_ok_forms-001, exit 0): SIN(66 RNUM RENAMES NUM) A1=0.479425 (sin 0.5), SIN(FUNCTION SQRT(NUM2 OF GRP)) A7=0.909297 (sin 2). Refuse half, q_bad_forms.cob --compile-only (exit 65): SIN(66 RENAMES NUM THRU NUM2) COBOL1627 class alphanumeric; SIN(88 ISONE) COBOL1639. 1985-only operand forms, q_special_regs.cob (runs/q_special_regs-003): LINAGE-COUNTER / PAGE-COUNTER / LINE-COUNTER accepted as numeric arguments with correct values. Later-edition classes at 85, q_later_forms.cob: SIN(USAGE POINTER) COBOL1627 class pointer plus COBOL0900 POINTER requires 2002. The 2002-gated ScreenIdentifierPlacement (Constructs.NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002) is not on the argument path (callers are identifier doors only), consistent with SIN(FUNCTION SQRT(..)) being accepted at 85. cite.py: 'OK §1989:A.2.39.3 AR1'; 'OK §1989:A.2.2 AR1'; 'OK §1985:VI.6.2.1 (6.2.1 Definition of an Arithmetic Expression) the text is in the clause'.
